q: At a seder on this holiday, families retell the story of the exodus from Egypt using a book called the Haggadah. They eat matzah, bitter herbs, and charoset, and they drink four cups of wine. For 10 points, name this eight-day spring festival of freedom from slavery.

This winter festival commemorates the rededication of the Temple in Jerusalem after the Maccabean revolt. Jewish families light one more candle each night on a special candelabrum and play with a spinning top called a dreidel. For 10 points, name this holiday also called the Festival of Lights.

This is the holiest day of the Jewish year, a day of fasting, prayer, and repentance. It falls ten days after Rosh Hashanah, and the services end with the sounding of a ram's horn. For 10 points, name this Day of Atonement.

This holiday opens the Jewish High Holy Days. It is the Jewish New Year and is celebrated with the blowing of the shofar and with apples dipped in honey to symbolize a sweet year. For 10 points, name this holiday that falls in early autumn and whose name means head of the year.

Jews observe this day of rest from Friday evening until Saturday night. Families light candles, say a blessing over wine, and eat braided bread called challah. Observant Jews avoid work on this day, as the Ten Commandments instruct. For 10 points, name this weekly holy day.

This building is the Jewish place of worship, where services are held and the Torah is read. It also serves as a place of study and community gathering. A cantor often leads the singing, and a rabbi often leads the congregation. For 10 points, name this house of prayer that is the Jewish counterpart of a church.

This title is given to a teacher and spiritual leader of a Jewish community. Such a person interprets Jewish law, leads services, and counsels congregants. The word means my master in Hebrew. For 10 points, name this position held by the leader of a synagogue.

This six-pointed shape of two overlapping triangles appears on the flag of Israel. It is also known by the name of a Hebrew king, and Nazi Germany forced Jews to wear it as a badge. For 10 points, name this symbol of Judaism.

This candelabrum with seven branches was used in the Temple in Jerusalem and is a symbol of Judaism. A version with nine branches is lit during Hanukkah. The emblem of the state of Israel includes this object. For 10 points, name this lamp stand.

This collection of rabbinic discussions of Jewish law and tradition includes the Mishnah and the Gemara. There are two versions, one compiled in Babylonia and one in the Land of Israel. For 10 points, name this central text of rabbinic Judaism, whose name means study.

God commands this man to leave his home in Ur and promises him descendants as numerous as the stars. He is told to sacrifice his son Isaac, but an angel stops him. He is a father of both Judaism and Islam. For 10 points, name this first of the three patriarchs.

According to Genesis, God told this man to build an ark to save his family and pairs of animals from a great flood. A dove returned to him with an olive branch. For 10 points, name this biblical figure whose sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

Moses received these laws on two stone tablets on Mount Sinai. They include rules against murder, theft, and lying, and they require keeping the Sabbath holy. For 10 points, name these ten rules given by God to the Israelites.

The second book of the Bible tells how the Israelites were enslaved in Egypt and then freed. It includes the burning bush, the ten plagues, and the parting of the Red Sea. For 10 points, name this book, whose name means going out.

As a boy, this man defeated the giant Goliath with a sling and a stone. He later became the second king of Israel, captured Jerusalem, and is credited with writing many psalms. For 10 points, name this king, whose name is on a six-pointed star.

The Bible says this king of Israel asked God for wisdom rather than riches. He is known for settling a dispute between two women who claimed the same baby, and for building the First Temple in Jerusalem. For 10 points, name this son of David.

This holiday celebrates the rescue of the Jews of Persia from the plot of the villain Haman. People read from a scroll, dress in costumes, give gifts of food, and make noise with groggers whenever Haman is named. For 10 points, name this joyous spring holiday.

This prophet was swallowed by a great fish after trying to flee from God's command to preach in Nineveh. He spent three days in its belly before being spit out onto dry land. For 10 points, name this biblical figure.

This prophet was thrown into a den of lions after he continued to pray to God despite a royal decree. He also interpreted dreams for Babylonian kings and read the writing on the wall at Belshazzar's feast. For 10 points, name this Hebrew prophet.

At age thirteen, a Jewish boy takes on the responsibilities of adulthood in this ceremony. He reads from the Torah in front of the congregation and often celebrates with a large party. The comparable ceremony for girls is called a bat mitzvah. For 10 points, name this coming-of-age ritual.

Jewish dietary laws, called by this word, forbid eating pork and shellfish and mixing meat with dairy. Food that follows these rules is considered fit to eat. For 10 points, give this word that describes food prepared in accordance with Jewish law.

On this fall holiday, Jews build temporary huts with roofs made of branches and eat meals inside them. The huts recall the shelters the Israelites used while wandering in the desert. Observers also wave a palm branch, myrtle, willow, and a citron. For 10 points, name this festival of booths.

This word is an acronym of the three sections of the Hebrew Bible: Torah, Nevi'im, and Ketuvim. It contains the same books that Christians call the Old Testament, though arranged differently. For 10 points, name this Jewish scripture.

This surviving retaining wall of the Second Temple complex in Jerusalem is the holiest place where Jews may pray. People tuck written prayers into its cracks. It is also called the Wailing Wall. For 10 points, name this ancient limestone wall.

Esau sold his birthright to this man for a bowl of stew. He later dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven and wrestled with an angel, after which he was given the name Israel. For 10 points, name this son of Isaac whose twelve sons founded the tribes of Israel.

His brothers sold this son of Jacob into slavery out of jealousy over his colorful coat. He rose to power in Egypt after interpreting the dreams of the pharaoh. For 10 points, name this biblical figure whose story is told at the end of Genesis.

This judge of Israel was famed for his great strength, which was linked to his uncut hair. Delilah betrayed him to the Philistines, and in the end he pulled down the pillars of a temple. For 10 points, name this biblical strongman.

This ram's horn is blown on Rosh Hashanah and at the end of Yom Kippur. The Bible says its sound was heard at Mount Sinai. It produces calls named tekiah, shevarim, and teruah. For 10 points, name this ancient instrument.
Answer these questions about the five books of Moses.
parts: Which book of the Bible, the first of all, tells of creation, Adam and Eve, and Noah?
Which fourth book of the Torah is named for the censuses of the Israelites in the wilderness?
Which fifth book of the Torah contains Moses' farewell speeches and the Shema?

q: Answer these questions about Passover.
parts: What flat, unleavened bread is eaten during Passover?
What is the name of the Passover ceremonial meal?
What name is given to the book read aloud during the meal that recounts the exodus?

q: Answer these questions about Jewish ritual objects.
parts: What small box containing a scroll is fixed to the doorposts of Jewish homes?
What fringed prayer shawl do Jewish men wear during morning prayers?
What small leather boxes containing Torah verses are strapped to the arm and forehead during weekday morning prayer?

q: Answer these questions about the matriarchs and patriarchs.
parts: Who was the wife of Abraham, who bore Isaac at an old age?
Which wife of Isaac was the mother of Jacob and Esau?
Which wife of Jacob was the mother of Joseph and Benjamin?

q: Answer these questions about biblical prophets.
parts: Which prophet is said to have been taken to heaven in a chariot of fire?
Which prophet, whose book is the first of the Latter Prophets, foresaw swords beaten into plowshares?
Which prophet is called the weeping prophet and is the traditional author of Lamentations?

q: Answer these questions about the branches of modern Judaism.
parts: Which branch of Judaism, the most traditional, strictly follows halakha, or Jewish law?
Which branch, founded in nineteenth-century Germany, adapted practices to modern life and emphasizes ethical teachings?
Which branch, between the other two, is associated with the Jewish Theological Seminary and holds to tradition while allowing change?

q: Answer these questions about women of the Hebrew Bible.
parts: Which woman, a Moabite, told her mother-in-law Naomi, wherever you go I will go?
Which prophet and judge led Israel with the general Barak and sang a famous victory song?
Which sister of Moses and Aaron led women in song after the crossing of the sea?

q: Answer these questions about Jewish life cycle events.
parts: What ritual circumcision performed on eight-day-old boys is known by what Hebrew name?
What name is given to the Jewish funeral week of mourning at home, which lasts seven days?
What word in Hebrew names the ritual bath used in conversion and before weddings?

q: Muslims believe this book was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad by the angel Gabriel over about twenty-three years. It is divided into 114 chapters called surahs, and it is recited in Arabic. Many Muslims memorize it in full. For 10 points, name this holy book of Islam.

This man received his first revelation in the Cave of Hira at about age forty. He preached in his hometown of Mecca, was forced to leave, and later returned in triumph. Muslims consider him the last prophet and add the phrase peace be upon him after his name. For 10 points, name this founder of Islam.

Muslims around the world face this city when they pray, and it is the destination of the annual pilgrimage. It is located in Saudi Arabia and is the birthplace of the Prophet Muhammad. Non-Muslims are not allowed to enter its sacred area. For 10 points, name this holiest city of Islam.

The Prophet Muhammad moved to this city in 622 after being persecuted in Mecca. It became the capital of the first Muslim community, and the Prophet is buried here under the Green Dome. For 10 points, name this second holiest city in Islam, located in Saudi Arabia.

During this ninth month of the Islamic calendar, Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. Families gather to break the fast each evening with a meal called iftar, and many attend special night prayers. For 10 points, name this holy month of fasting that ends with Eid al-Fitr.

This holiday marks the end of Ramadan. Muslims gather for a special prayer, give charity, wear new clothes, and share sweets with family and friends. Its name means festival of breaking the fast. For 10 points, name this three-day celebration.

This holiday honors the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son at God's command. Muslims often sacrifice an animal and share the meat with the poor. It falls during the pilgrimage to Mecca. For 10 points, name this festival of sacrifice, which comes about two months after the other Eid.

Every able Muslim who can afford it is expected to make this journey to Mecca at least once. Pilgrims wear simple white clothing, walk around the Kaaba, and stand on the plain of Arafat. For 10 points, name this pilgrimage that is the fifth pillar of Islam.

This cube-shaped building draped in a black cloth sits at the center of the Great Mosque of Mecca. Muslims believe it was built by Abraham and his son Ishmael. Pilgrims walk around it seven times. For 10 points, name this holiest shrine in Islam toward which Muslims face when they pray.

Muslims gather in this building for communal prayers, especially on Fridays. It has a prayer hall, a washing area for ritual purification, and a niche pointing toward Mecca. For 10 points, name this Islamic house of worship.

The call to prayer is traditionally given from the top of this tall, slender tower attached to a mosque. Some of these towers are very ornate, and a mosque may have several. For 10 points, name this architectural feature of mosques.

This word is the title for the person who leads prayers in a mosque. It also names a leader of the Muslim community, and Shia Muslims use it for a line of spiritual successors to Muhammad. For 10 points, give this term for a prayer leader.

The first pillar of Islam is this declaration of faith. It states that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the messenger of God. Saying it with sincerity makes someone a Muslim. For 10 points, name this Islamic creed.

This is one of the five pillars of Islam, a form of required almsgiving. Muslims who are able to pay donate a set portion of their savings each year to the poor. For 10 points, name this Islamic obligation that means purification.

This branch of Islam, whose name refers to the Prophet's example, makes up the large majority of Muslims worldwide. It holds that the community chose Abu Bakr as the first caliph. For 10 points, name this branch that is the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

The followers of this branch of Islam believe Muhammad's cousin and son-in-law Ali was his rightful successor. Their name comes from a phrase meaning party of Ali. Iran and Iraq have large populations of this branch. For 10 points, name this second-largest branch of Islam.

The Islamic calendar begins with this event in 622, when Muhammad and his followers traveled from Mecca to Medina. The word means migration. For 10 points, name this journey that marks year one of the Islamic calendar.

This word names the collected sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad as recorded by his companions. Muslims use it, along with the Quran, as a source of guidance. For 10 points, give this term for such a reported tradition.

This term refers to the body of Islamic law, derived from the Quran, the Hadith, and scholarly reasoning. It guides worship, family matters, and many other areas of life. For 10 points, name this religious law of Islam, whose name means the path.

After Muhammad died, this word came to be used for the successor who led the Muslim community. Four of them are called the rightly guided ones. For 10 points, give this title of the political and religious head of the Islamic state, translated as successor.

This close friend of Muhammad and father of his wife Aisha became the first caliph in 632. He put down rebellions in Arabia and had the Quran gathered into written form. For 10 points, name this first of the rightly guided caliphs.
This cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad was the fourth caliph. Shia Muslims regard him as the first imam. He was the husband of Fatima and father of Hasan and Husayn. For 10 points, name this man.

This wealthy merchant of Mecca became the first wife of Muhammad. She supported him after his first revelation and was the first person to accept his message. For 10 points, name this woman, who was the mother of Fatima.

This Muslim sultan of Egypt and Syria recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187. He was known for his chivalry and was respected by Richard the Lionheart. For 10 points, name this Kurdish leader.

This symbol of a curved moon and a star appears on the flags of several Muslim-majority countries, such as Turkey and Pakistan. It is widely used to represent Islam, although it is not a religious symbol from the time of the Prophet. For 10 points, name this moon shape.

Under Islamic dietary laws, food that is permitted is described by this Arabic term, which means lawful. Pork and alcohol are forbidden. For 10 points, give this term, used to describe meat slaughtered in the prescribed way.
This person stands in a minaret or inside a mosque and calls Muslims to prayer five times a day. Bilal, a freed slave, was the first to do it. For 10 points, name this role, whose call is the adhan.
This Arabic word refers to the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca, which Muslims face when praying. A niche called the mihrab in a mosque shows it. For 10 points, name this direction of prayer.

Muslims believe the Quran was first revealed to Muhammad on this Night of Power during Ramadan. It is said to be better than a thousand months. Many Muslims spend it in prayer. For 10 points, name this night, which falls on one of the last odd nights of Ramadan.

This golden-domed shrine in Jerusalem was completed in 691 under the caliph Abd al-Malik. It stands on the Temple Mount and encloses a sacred rock from which Muslims believe Muhammad ascended to heaven. For 10 points, name this Islamic monument.
Answer these questions about prayer in Islam.
parts: How many times a day do observant Muslims perform the required prayers?
What ritual washing of hands, face, and feet is done before prayer?
On what day of the week do Muslims gather at the mosque for the main congregational prayer?

q: Answer these questions about the structure of the Quran.
parts: How many chapters are in the Quran?
What is the Arabic word for a chapter of the Quran?
What short opening chapter of the Quran is recited in every prayer unit?

q: Answer these questions about prophets in Islam.
parts: Which prophet, called Ibrahim in Arabic, is honored in Islam as the builder of the Kaaba?
Which prophet, known as Musa in Arabic, is the one most often named in the Quran?
Which prophet, called Isa in Arabic, is revered by Muslims as a messenger born to the Virgin Maryam?

q: Answer these questions about Islamic empires.
parts: Which empire, centered at Constantinople, captured that city in 1453 and ruled much of the Middle East until the twentieth century?
Which Muslim dynasty, founded by Babur, ruled much of India and built the Taj Mahal?
Which Muslim dynasty, with its capital at Baghdad, followed the Umayyads and ruled during the golden age of Islam?

q: Answer these questions about features of mosque architecture.
parts: What rounded roof is a common feature of mosque architecture?
What niche in the wall of a mosque shows the direction of prayer?
What stepped pulpit in a mosque is used for the Friday sermon?

q: Answer these questions about the Islamic year.
parts: Which month of the Islamic calendar is known for fasting?
Which month is the first of the Islamic year and includes the day of Ashura?
What Arabic word names the lesser pilgrimage to Mecca, which can be made at any time of the year?

q: Answer these questions about Muslim scholars and travelers.
parts: Which Moroccan traveler of the fourteenth century wrote a famous account of his journeys across the Muslim world?
Which Persian scholar, known in Europe as Avicenna, wrote The Canon of Medicine?
Which Persian mathematician's name gave us the word algorithm?

q: Answer these questions about Muslim practice and belief.
parts: What is the Arabic word for God used by Muslims?
What Arabic word, meaning forbidden, describes actions or foods not permitted in Islam?
What Arabic word means the oneness of God and is the central idea of Islam?

q: This prince was born in Lumbini, in what is now Nepal, and grew up in a palace shielded from suffering. After seeing an old man, a sick man, and a corpse, he gave up his wealth to seek enlightenment. He attained it beneath a fig tree after long meditation. For 10 points, name this founder of Buddhism, known by a title meaning the awakened one.

Families celebrate this autumn festival of lights by setting out small oil lamps called diyas and lighting fireworks. It honors the goddess Lakshmi and celebrates the victory of light over darkness. Many Hindus, Sikhs, and Jains observe it. For 10 points, name this holiday also known as the Festival of Lights in India.

During this spring festival, participants throw colored powder and water at each other in streets and parks. It marks the arrival of spring and celebrates the triumph of good over evil. For 10 points, name this Hindu festival of colors.

This Hindu god is the preserver in the trimurti, along with Brahma and Shiva. He is said to have come to earth in ten avatars, including Rama and Krishna. He is often shown with blue skin, resting on a serpent. For 10 points, name this deity.

This Hindu god is called the destroyer and is often shown with a third eye, a trident, and a cobra around his neck. The Ganges is said to flow from his hair. For 10 points, name this deity whose dance of destruction and creation is shown in the Nataraja form.

This Hindu god has the head of an elephant and is worshiped as the remover of obstacles. He is the son of Shiva and Parvati, and he is often depicted with a broken tusk and a mouse. For 10 points, name this deity honored at the start of new ventures.

This blue-skinned Hindu deity is the eighth avatar of Vishnu. He is known for playing the flute, stealing butter as a child, and serving as the charioteer of Arjuna. For 10 points, name this god who teaches in the Bhagavad Gita.

This text is a 700-verse section of the Mahabharata in which the warrior Arjuna receives advice from his charioteer on the battlefield of Kurukshetra. It discusses duty, devotion, and action. For 10 points, name this Hindu scripture, whose name means the Song of God.

These are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, composed in Sanskrit and made up of four collections, including the Rigveda. They contain hymns, rituals, and philosophical ideas. For 10 points, name these ancient scriptures, whose name means knowledge.

In Hindu and Buddhist belief, this principle holds that a person's actions have consequences that affect their future, including later lives. Good deeds bring good results and bad deeds bring bad results. For 10 points, name this law of cause and effect whose name means action in Sanskrit.

This belief, shared by Hindus, Buddhists, and Jains, holds that the soul is born again into a new body after death. The cycle continues until a person achieves liberation. For 10 points, name this idea, also called rebirth or samsara.

Hindus believe bathing in this river washes away sins. Millions gather on its banks at Varanasi and at the Kumbh Mela. Ashes of the dead are often scattered in it. For 10 points, name this holy river of India.

The Buddha's first sermon laid out four truths, beginning with the idea that life involves suffering. It ties suffering to craving and states that it can end by following a path. For 10 points, name this set of core Buddhist teachings, whose number is in the name.

This path to ending suffering in Buddhism has eight parts: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. For 10 points, name this set of practices that is the fourth of the Four Noble Truths.

In Buddhism, this is the state of freedom from suffering and the cycle of rebirth. The word means blowing out, like a flame going out. For 10 points, name this goal of the Buddhist path, which is the final release.

The Buddha is said to have gained enlightenment while meditating beneath this tree at Bodh Gaya. A descendant of the original still stands there today. For 10 points, name this tree sacred to Buddhists, a type of fig.

Tibetan Buddhists believe this title holder is the reincarnation of a compassionate bodhisattva. The current holder fled Tibet in 1959 and lives in exile in India. For 10 points, give this title of the spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism.

This school of Buddhism, which spread from China to Japan, emphasizes meditation rather than study of scriptures. It is known for riddles called koans and for rock gardens in temples. For 10 points, name this form of Buddhism.

This Chinese philosopher is the traditional author of the Tao Te Ching. His name means old master, and legend says he wrote the book before leaving China on a water buffalo. For 10 points, name this founder of Taoism.

This short text of about 81 chapters is the central book of Taoism. It teaches that one should live in harmony with a natural force called the Way, and it praises simplicity and humility. For 10 points, name this classic whose title means the Way and its Power.

This symbol of a circle divided into black and white halves, each with a dot of the other color, represents balance in Taoism. The two halves are opposites that depend on each other. For 10 points, name this Chinese symbol, called taijitu.

This Chinese thinker taught that society works best when people respect their parents, elders, and rulers. He lived around 500 BC, and his ideas became the basis of an ethical system in East Asia. For 10 points, name this philosopher.

This collection of sayings and short dialogues of Confucius and his disciples was compiled by his followers after his death. It begins with the line: is it not a pleasure to learn and to practice what is learned? For 10 points, name this central Confucian text.

This indigenous religion of Japan honors spirits called kami and has shrines at places of natural beauty. Its rituals emphasize purity, and many Japanese couples hold weddings at its shrines. For 10 points, name this religion that, unlike Buddhism, originated in Japan.

This red gate marks the entrance to a Shinto shrine and is a boundary between the ordinary world and sacred space. A famous one stands in the water at Itsukushima Shrine on Miyajima. For 10 points, name this type of Japanese gateway.

This ancient Sanskrit epic tells of a prince exiled to a forest with his wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana. Sita is kidnapped by the demon king Ravana, and the monkey Hanuman helps rescue her. For 10 points, name this epic attributed to the poet Valmiki.
This Hindu goddess of wealth and good fortune is the wife of Vishnu. She is often shown seated on a lotus and holding gold coins. Many people honor her at Diwali. For 10 points, name this goddess.

This Sanskrit syllable is considered the sacred sound of the universe in Hinduism and is also used in Buddhism and Jainism. It is chanted at the beginning of prayers and meditation and is often written in a special symbol. For 10 points, name this mantra.

This largest religion of India has no single founder and no single scripture. Its followers worship many forms of one ultimate reality, called Brahman, including Vishnu, Shiva, and Devi. For 10 points, name this religion, followed by about a billion people, which includes the practice of yoga.

This dome-shaped Buddhist monument holds relics of the Buddha or of revered monks. Pilgrims walk around it clockwise as a form of devotion. A famous example stands at Sanchi in India, and the form influenced the pagoda. For 10 points, name this type of structure, called a chorten in Tibet.
Answer these questions about the Hindu gods.
parts: Which Hindu god is the creator in the trimurti, alongside Vishnu and Shiva?
Which monkey god is the devoted helper of Rama?
Which Hindu goddess of learning and the arts is often shown with a veena?

q: Answer these questions about the life of the Buddha.
parts: At which town in the Indian state of Bihar is the Buddha said to have found enlightenment?
At which deer park near Varanasi did the Buddha give his first sermon?
In which city, in northern India, is the Buddha traditionally said to have died?

q: Answer these questions about Buddhist traditions.
parts: Which branch of Buddhism, the oldest surviving, is dominant in Sri Lanka and Thailand?
Which branch, whose name means great vehicle, spread to China, Korea, and Japan?
Which branch, found in Tibet, uses ritual and tantric methods and is also called the diamond vehicle?

q: Answer these questions about Confucianism.
parts: What word describes the respect that children owe to their parents in Confucian thought?
Which Confucian thinker, whose name is a Latinized form of Meng Zi, argued that human nature is good?
What Chinese word for humaneness or benevolence is the chief virtue of Confucius?

q: Answer these questions about Taoism.
parts: What Chinese word, translated as the Way, gives Taoism its name?
Which Taoist philosopher wrote a book named for himself that contains the story of the butterfly dream?
What Taoist idea, meaning effortless action, advises acting in harmony with nature?

q: Answer these questions about the Hindu epics and scriptures.
parts: Which giant Sanskrit epic, the longest poem in the world, tells of a war between the Pandavas and the Kauravas?
Which philosophical texts, whose name means sitting near a teacher, are the end part of the Vedas?
Which Indian sage is traditionally credited with composing the longest Sanskrit epic and compiling the Vedas?

q: Answer these questions about Hindu concepts.
parts: What word means a person's duty or righteous way of life in Hinduism?
What term refers to liberation from the cycle of birth and death?
What term describes the traditional division of Hindu society into four classes?

q: Answer these questions about Hindu festivals.
parts: What nine-night festival, held in autumn, honors the goddess Durga?
On which festival do sisters tie a thread bracelet on their brothers' wrists?
What huge Hindu pilgrimage festival is held every twelve years at four river sites?

q: This religion was founded in the Punjab region around 1500. Its followers worship one God, reject caste distinctions, and keep their hair uncut under a turban. Their temples are called gurdwaras, where free communal meals are served. For 10 points, name this religion whose scripture is the Guru Granth Sahib.

This man was the first of the ten Sikh gurus. Born in the Punjab in 1469, he taught that there is one God and that all people are equal. He traveled widely, spreading his message through songs and poems. For 10 points, name this founder of Sikhism.

This gold-covered Sikh house of worship in Amritsar sits in the middle of a sacred pool. Visitors cover their heads and remove their shoes before entering, and the Guru Granth Sahib is read inside around the clock. For 10 points, name this shrine, also called Harmandir Sahib.

Sikhs treat this holy book as their living guru. Compiled by Guru Arjan and later expanded by Guru Gobind Singh, it contains hymns by Sikh gurus and by saints of other traditions. For 10 points, name this scripture, which is kept on a throne in every gurdwara.

Guru Gobind Singh created this order of initiated Sikhs in 1699 at Anandpur. Members are expected to wear the five articles of faith and to follow a code of conduct. For 10 points, give this term for the Sikh community of the pure.

These are five items observed by initiated Sikhs, each beginning with the same letter in Punjabi: uncut hair, a comb, a steel bracelet, a short sword, and special undergarments. For 10 points, give the name by which this group of five articles of faith is known.

This ancient Indian religion teaches nonviolence toward all living things. Its monks sometimes sweep the ground before them and wear cloths over their mouths to avoid harming small creatures. It has twenty-four teachers called tirthankaras. For 10 points, name this religion, found mostly in India.

This man, a contemporary of the Buddha, is considered the twenty-fourth and last tirthankara of Jainism. He gave up royal life, wandered as an ascetic, and taught the importance of nonviolence. For 10 points, name this teacher whose name means great hero.
This word, meaning nonviolence, is a basic principle of Jainism, Buddhism, and Hinduism. Mahatma Gandhi made it a central part of his philosophy of resistance. For 10 points, give this Sanskrit term.

Founded in nineteenth-century Persia, this religion teaches the unity of all religions and all humanity. Its followers consider Baha'u'llah to be its prophet. Its houses of worship have nine sides and are open to all faiths. For 10 points, name this religion.

This ancient Persian religion is named for a prophet who taught that the world is a struggle between truth and falsehood. Its followers keep sacred fires burning in their temples. It was the main religion of the Persian Empire. For 10 points, name this faith, which has about a hundred thousand followers worldwide, many of them called Parsis in India.

This Persian prophet is said to have received a vision from the supreme god and wrote hymns called the Gathas. He lived in ancient Iran thousands of years ago, and his teachings emphasize good thoughts, good words, and good deeds. For 10 points, name this founder of a religion that bears his name.

This is the supreme god of Zoroastrianism, whose name means wise lord. He is opposed by the destructive spirit Angra Mainyu, and the prophet Zoroaster is said to have received revelations from him. For 10 points, name this creator god.

This Jamaican-born religious movement considers Haile Selassie, the emperor of Ethiopia, to be a divine figure. Its members often wear dreadlocks and avoid certain foods, and reggae music is associated with it. For 10 points, name this movement, whose followers use the colors red, gold, and green.

This modern nature religion honors a goddess and a horned god and celebrates festivals that mark the turning of the seasons. Many of its practitioners call themselves witches. For 10 points, name this religion associated with Gerald Gardner.

These priests of the ancient Celts served as judges, teachers, and religious leaders. According to Roman writers, they conducted rites in sacred oak groves and cut mistletoe with a golden sickle. For 10 points, name this class of priests.

In Egyptian myth, this god of the dead and the underworld was killed by his brother Set. His wife Isis revived him, and he judged souls in the afterlife. He is often shown green or black, wrapped like a mummy. For 10 points, name this Egyptian god.

This Egyptian sun god sailed across the sky each day in a boat and traveled through the underworld at night. He was often depicted as a man with the head of a falcon and a sun disk. For 10 points, name this chief god of ancient Egypt.

This Egyptian god with a jackal head guided the dead and oversaw mummification. He weighed the hearts of the dead against the feather of truth, and the god Thoth recorded the result. For 10 points, name this deity.
This king of the Greek gods wielded thunderbolts and ruled from Mount Olympus. He was the son of Cronus and Rhea, and his wife was Hera. For 10 points, name this god, called Jupiter by the Romans.

This one-eyed Norse god, ruler of Asgard, gave up an eye in return for wisdom. He rides an eight-legged horse named Sleipnir, and his ravens Huginn and Muninn bring him news. For 10 points, name this chief god of Norse mythology.

This Norse god of thunder wields the hammer Mjolnir and rides a chariot pulled by goats. He fights giants and the serpent Jormungandr. For 10 points, name this god, after whom a day of the week is named.

In Norse belief, brave warriors who die in battle are taken to this hall in Asgard. They fight each day and feast each night, preparing for Ragnarok. For 10 points, name this hall presided over by Odin.

This feathered serpent god of the Aztecs was associated with the wind, learning, and the morning star. Some stories say the Aztec ruler Moctezuma thought Hernan Cortes might be this figure returned. For 10 points, name this deity, called Kukulkan by the Maya.
This belief, found in many indigenous cultures, holds that animals, plants, rivers, and mountains have spirits. The word comes from the Latin for soul. For 10 points, name this type of belief system.

This religion of Haiti combines West African beliefs with elements of Catholicism. Its practitioners honor spirits called lwa and hold ceremonies led by priests called houngans. For 10 points, name this religion, which is often misrepresented in films.

This looped Egyptian symbol resembles a cross with a handle and means life. Many Egyptian gods and pharaohs are shown holding one, and it often appears in tomb paintings and jewelry. For 10 points, name this symbol.

Each year on November 1 and 2, families in Mexico build altars with marigolds, candles, and sugar skulls to honor dead relatives. It blends indigenous traditions with the Catholic holidays of All Saints and All Souls. For 10 points, name this holiday, called Dia de los Muertos in Spanish.

This kind of religious practitioner, found in Siberia, Korea, and many other cultures, is believed to enter a trance and communicate with the spirit world. The word is Evenki in origin. For 10 points, name this type of healer and spiritual intermediary.

This ancient circle of standing stones on Salisbury Plain in England may have been used for religious ceremonies. Many people gather there at the summer solstice, when the sun rises over the Heel Stone. For 10 points, name this prehistoric monument.

q: This organelle has a double membrane, contains its own small circular DNA, and carries out most of the steps of cellular respiration. Its inner membrane is folded into cristae. For 10 points, name this "powerhouse of the cell" that makes most of its ATP.

This molecule is found in the nucleus and is shaped like a twisted ladder, or double helix. Its rungs are made of the base pairs adenine with thymine and guanine with cytosine. Watson and Crick described its structure in 1953. For 10 points, name this molecule that carries genetic information.

Cells of this kind lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Their DNA floats in a region called the nucleoid, and they include the domains Bacteria and Archaea. For 10 points, name this simple type of cell, contrasted with eukaryotic cells.

This process takes place in chloroplasts. It uses light energy, water, and carbon dioxide to make glucose and releases oxygen as a byproduct. For 10 points, name this process by which plants make their own food.

In this stage of the cell cycle, a cell grows and copies its DNA before it divides. It makes up the majority of the time in the life of a typical cell. For 10 points, name this stage that comes before mitosis.

These proteins act as biological catalysts, speeding up chemical reactions in living things without being used up. Amylase and lactase are examples, and each one fits a specific substrate at its active site. For 10 points, name these proteins whose names usually end in "-ase."

This system of the human body includes the heart, blood vessels, and blood. Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins return it. For 10 points, name this system that transports oxygen and nutrients around the body.

This is the term for the passive movement of water across a semipermeable membrane from an area of low solute concentration to an area of high solute concentration. A cell placed in pure water will swell because of it. For 10 points, name this process.

Gregor Mendel studied inheritance by crossing varieties of this plant in a monastery garden. He tracked traits such as seed shape and flower color. For 10 points, name this plant, whose pods hold the seeds Mendel counted.

In this kind of cell division, one cell divides to make two genetically identical daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes. Its phases are prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase. For 10 points, name this process used for growth and repair of body tissues.

This is the green pigment found in chloroplasts that absorbs mostly red and blue light. It reflects green light, which is why leaves look green. For 10 points, name this pigment essential to photosynthesis.

This organelle is surrounded by a double membrane called an envelope that is perforated by pores. It contains the chromatin and a dense region called the nucleolus, where ribosomes are assembled. For 10 points, name this organelle that houses most of a eukaryotic cell's DNA.

These structures are made of ribosomal RNA and protein and are found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. They may float free in the cytoplasm or attach to the rough endoplasmic reticulum. For 10 points, name these tiny structures where translation builds proteins.

A typical example of this process begins with an enzyme called helicase that unzips the double helix. DNA polymerase then adds complementary nucleotides to each strand. Because each new molecule keeps one old strand, it is called semiconservative. For 10 points, name this process in which DNA is copied.

This is the term for a pair of alleles that are identical, such as AA or aa. Organisms with this condition are said to be pure for the trait. For 10 points, name this genetic condition, the opposite of heterozygous.

Stacks of flattened sacs called cisternae make up this organelle, which receives vesicles from the endoplasmic reticulum. It modifies, sorts, and packages proteins for secretion. For 10 points, name this organelle named for an Italian scientist who described it in 1898.

In this process, the sequence of a gene is used to build a strand of messenger RNA by the enzyme RNA polymerase. It occurs in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. For 10 points, name this first step of gene expression, which comes before translation.

Hemoglobin in these cells carries oxygen. Mature ones in humans have no nucleus and are shaped like biconcave disks. For 10 points, name these cells, also called erythrocytes, that give blood its red color.

This kingdom includes mushrooms, molds, and yeasts. Its members have cell walls made of chitin and absorb nutrients from their surroundings. For 10 points, name this kingdom of organisms that are neither plants nor animals.

Charles Darwin visited these Pacific islands on the HMS Beagle and observed finches and tortoises that differed from island to island. These observations helped shape his theory of natural selection. For 10 points, name these islands belonging to Ecuador.

In this process, water moves up a plant and evaporates from tiny pores on the underside of leaves. The pores are called stomata and are controlled by guard cells. For 10 points, name this loss of water vapor from plants.

This kind of relationship benefits both species involved. Examples include bees pollinating flowers and the bacteria in your gut that help digest food. For 10 points, name this kind of symbiosis, contrasted with parasitism and commensalism.

The Punnett square is used to predict the results of genetic crosses. If two heterozygous parents, Bb and Bb, are crossed, the expected ratio of dominant to recessive phenotypes is this. For 10 points, give this ratio.

These tiny air sacs at the ends of the bronchioles are where gas exchange takes place in the lungs. They are surrounded by networks of capillaries. For 10 points, name these structures where oxygen enters the blood.

This structure of the cell is a fluid mosaic made of a bilayer of phospholipids with embedded proteins. The heads of its molecules are hydrophilic and the tails are hydrophobic. Cholesterol helps regulate its fluidity. For 10 points, name this boundary that controls what enters and leaves a cell.

This cycle is also called the citric acid cycle. It takes place in the mitochondrial matrix, where acetyl CoA combines with oxaloacetate to form citrate. It produces NADH, FADH2, and carbon dioxide. For 10 points, name this cycle named for a German-British biochemist.

The Hardy-Weinberg principle describes how common gene variants are in a population that is not evolving. Its equation is p squared plus 2pq plus q squared equals one, where p and q stand for these quantities. For 10 points, name these two things whose frequencies sum to one in the equation p plus q equals one.

These organelles in animal cells are filled with digestive enzymes and work at an acidic pH. A disease such as Tay-Sachs results when one of their enzymes is missing. For 10 points, name these organelles that break down worn-out cell parts and ingested material.

This type of cell division produces four haploid cells from one diploid cell. Crossing over occurs during its first prophase, and homologous chromosomes separate in its first anaphase. For 10 points, name this cell division that produces gametes.

Louis Pasteur's swan-neck flask experiments helped disprove this old idea, the notion that living things can arise from nonliving matter. For 10 points, name this idea, which Francesco Redi also tested with jars of meat and flies.

q: This element has atomic number 1 and is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe. Two atoms of it bond with one of oxygen to form water. For 10 points, name this element with the symbol H.

This noble gas is used to fill balloons because it is lighter than air and does not burn. It is the second lightest element and has atomic number 2. For 10 points, name this gas, which makes a person's voice squeaky when inhaled.

This scale runs from 0 to 14 and measures how acidic or basic a solution is. Pure water sits at 7 on it, lemon juice is far lower, and household bleach is far higher. Litmus paper and universal indicator are used to estimate readings on it. For 10 points, name this scale.

The three states of matter most often seen on Earth are solid, liquid, and this one. Particles of it are far apart, move quickly, and fill any container. For 10 points, name this state of matter that includes air.
In this kind of bond, two atoms share pairs of electrons. Water molecules and methane molecules are held together by it. For 10 points, name this type of bond, contrasted with the ionic type.

This is the smallest particle of an element that still has the properties of that element. It has a nucleus of protons and neutrons surrounded by electrons. For 10 points, name this basic unit of matter.

Table salt, whose formula is NaCl, is made of sodium and this other element. This yellow-green gas is a poisonous halogen with atomic number 17. It is added in small amounts to swimming pools and drinking water to kill germs. For 10 points, name this element.

This is the process in which a solid turns directly into a gas without becoming a liquid first. Dry ice does this at room temperature, and so does snow on a cold, dry, sunny day. The reverse process is called deposition. For 10 points, name this change of state.
This metal is liquid at room temperature and was once used in thermometers. Its symbol Hg comes from a Latin name meaning "liquid silver." For 10 points, name this element, also called quicksilver.

This is the name for a substance made of two or more different elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio. Water and carbon dioxide are examples. For 10 points, give this term, contrasted with a mixture.

Atoms of the same element that have different numbers of neutrons are called these. They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers. Carbon-12 and carbon-14 are examples, and the latter is used in dating ancient objects. For 10 points, name these variants of an element.

Dmitri Mendeleev arranged elements by increasing atomic mass in the first widely accepted version of this chart. He left gaps for elements that had not yet been discovered. For 10 points, name this chart whose columns are called groups.
